facts.claim: Wikipedia says Edsger Dijkstra conceived his shortest-path algorithm in 1956, in about twenty minutes on a café terrace, and published it in 1959.
Wikipedia says breadth-first search can be seen as Dijkstra’s algorithm on a graph whose roads carry no weights.
Wikipedia says Hart, Nilsson and Raphael published A* in 1968, and that with a guess that never overestimates, it returns a shortest path.
Wikipedia says weighted A*, which multiplies the guess by a weight ε above 1, finds a path costing at most ε times the cheapest.
Google’s Maps blog (September 2020) says it combines historical traffic patterns with live conditions, and reroutes you around jams and incidents.
Wikipedia says road networks have tens of millions of junctions, too many for plain Dijkstra; contraction hierarchies add shortcuts ahead of time, and queries take microseconds.
Wikipedia cites Geisberger, Sanders, Schultes and Delling’s 2008 paper for contraction hierarchies.
The open-source OSRM route engine, run on OpenStreetMap data, offers two preprocessing pipelines: contraction hierarchies and multi-level Dijkstra.
